headline: Residents want parking placards back as plate readers ticket visitors to people with disabilities.
summary: Andy Varela, chair of the Ordinances, Licenses and Legal Affairs committee, is working with David Kuchowski to set up a committee meeting on a hybrid system of placards and electronic plate readers. A separate proposal would let the building inspector, with the ADA coordinator, decide certain disability-related zoning requests without zoning board review. That proposal stays in committee and still needs approval from the full council and the planning and zoning board.
discussion: Parking placards and plate readers: Residents said plate readers ticket visitors, nurses, and guests even when a placard is displayed, and asked the city to bring placards back. One speaker said they would write to the mayor's office and copy David Kuchowski and the council.

Accessible activities programs: The summer bash drew only two children. The inclusion sports program cost each family $150 for a six-week session, a presenter said, and members discussed grants and the donation account to lower fees.

Reasonable accommodation zoning: A proposal would let the building inspector, with the ADA coordinator, approve reasonable accommodation requests without going to the zoning board. A resident said the current process requires disclosing medical information and notifying neighbors, which costs money.

Salem Street intersection rebuild: The rebuilt intersection at Salem Street and Lafayette Place was built over the summer with a straighter path to the crosswalk and a crosswalk that does not extend into Lafayette Place. Utilities kept the crosswalk from moving farther up Salem Street.
